The paper does not document the exact aggregation implementation beyond stating mean aggregation and concatenation.

The precise KMeans initialization, distance metric, iteration schedule, and UMAP settings are unspecified.
The ITC, ITG, and ITM objective-specific tensor schedules and loss implementations are not fully specified.

The paper contains contradictory statements about image-encoder trainability: several sections describe it as frozen or unchanged, while the training protocol states that the full architecture is optimized end-to-end.
The paper does not establish whether the image-level and site-level representations in perturbation analysis are equivalent.
The paper does not specify the exact grouping-key representation linking images or sites to wells and wells to identical perturbation conditions.
The paper does not specify the exact batch/plate correspondence tensor used when computing cross-batch feature distances for IMAD.

operation_proposals.why_no_existing_operation: The paper documents Cellpose-based cell-instance segmentation followed by spatial cropping. The catalog primitives can select or partition values and can pad sequences, but none represents instance segmentation followed by spatial cropping.
The paper explicitly averages feature vectors across cells, images, wells, or query embeddings. Addition, concatenation, and learned projection do not represent arithmetic mean aggregation.
The reconstruction route applies a binary mask through element-wise occlusion of visual-token embeddings. Selection, indexed update, and augmentation do not express this documented masking algebra.
The image encoder is a complete ViT sequence encoder. The available attention and projection primitives do not establish the encoder's complete layer schedule or tensor transformation.

The Q-Former combines shared self-attention, cross-attention, query parameters, and text-related modes, while the paper does not establish a complete ordered decomposition suitable for the available primitives.
KMeans assigns samples through iterative centroid estimation and distance-based reassignment, which is not represented by learned projection, ranking, or selection.
UMAP is a nonlinear manifold embedding with neighborhood graph construction and optimization. The catalog's learned projection and reshape operations do not represent that algorithm.

evidence.quote: During pre-training, scMIR is trained on paired single-cell images and structured textual captions to enable text-guided visual representation learning.

Specifically, we use the ViTg/14 vision transformer from EVA-CLIP [69] as the image encoder. Freezing the image encoder allows scMIR to leverage pretrained visual priors, reduce computational cost, and limit the number of trainable parameters, facilitating efficient adaptation to singlecell microscopy image-text pairs.
During pretraining, the full scMIR architecture, consisting of the  image  encoder,  Q-Former,  and  the  proposed  image  reconstruction  module,  is optimized  end-to-end.
The  image  encoder  follows  the  standard  BLIP-2 configuration and remains unchanged throughout this work.
For cpg0000, full-field images were segmented into single-cell  instances  using  the  Cellpose  [1]  framework,  with  the  Hoechst  channel serving as the nuclear reference.
We  curated  six  publicly  available  microscopy  datasets  for  multimodal  pretraining, including  LIVECell,  cpg0000,  PBC,  HPA,  HepG2,  and  B\_ALL.

evidence.quote: The Q-Former is a trainable query-based transformer that maps high-dimensional visual features into a compact set of embeddings suitable for alignment with textual descriptions.

In our implementation, we use 32 learnable query embeddings, each with a hidden dimension of 768. Queries interact through self-attention and attend to the frozen image features via cross-attention, selectively extracting the most text-relevant visual information.
ITC encourages alignment between image and text representations by maximizing their mutual similarity while contrasting with negative pairs.
The ITG objective trains the model to generate textual descriptions conditioned on image features.
Hard  negative  mining  is applied to select informative unmatched pairs.
The extracted visual embeddings form the foundation for subsequent cross-modal representation learning.

evidence.quote: In downstream applications, the model takes only single-cell microscopy images as input and  outputs  task-agnostic  image  embeddings.

For cell classification tasks, datasets containing full-field microscopy images are first processed by cell segmentation to obtain single-cell images. Single-cell representations are extracted using the pretrained models and then aggregated by average pooling to obtain image-level features.

Fullfield images were processed using the same preprocessing pipeline as in pretraining to maintain consistency, except for DIBaS, which contains bacterial images, and CM4AI, which includes only a limited number of cells; neither dataset underwent single-cell segmentation.
